key_insight: LLMs can often spot and correct misconceptions in a first medical reply, but their ability drops sharply across follow-up turns in multi-turn conversations.
clinical_relevance: In patient-facing settings, inconsistent handling of false assumptions could reinforce misunderstanding and lead to less safe, less reliable medical guidance over time.
method: Built ThReadMed-QA from real AskDocs threads
Dataset includes 2,437 patient-physician conversations and 8,204 question-answer pairs
Compared five LLMs with a rubric-based LLM-as-a-Judge that scored misconception detection and correction
evidence_signal: GPT-5 and Claude-Haiku were about 85% correct on initial misconception questions, but fell to roughly 50% after two follow-up turns; oracle tests showed error propagation explains much of the decline.
watch_item: Results come from one dataset and one rubric-based evaluation setup, so real-world performance may vary across specialties, prompts, and clinical communication styles.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
